overview: BLIS Technologies is a Dunedin, New Zealand-based, 25-year-old developer and commercialiser of proprietary oral probiotic bacterial strains, principally BLIS K12 (Streptococcus salivarius K12) and BLIS M18, sold both as an ingredient to third-party consumer-health brands (B2B, majority of revenue and growing fastest) and as BLIS's own finished consumer products (B2C). Revenue is small ($14.7m FY26, up 16% YoY) and geographically diversified (North America 31%, EMEA 30%, Asia Pacific ex-NZ 24%, New Zealand 15%), but the company remains a nano-cap: FY26 EBITDA margin was only 6% (8% underlying) after eight years growing revenue from $8.2m (FY19), and the market capitalisation has re-rated to roughly NZ$28-29m at a ~$0.02-0.024 share price against ~1.28 billion shares on issue, following a strong Q1 FY27 trading update.

business_model.summary: BLIS licenses/sells its patented probiotic strains as raw ingredients to third-party manufacturers (ingredient sales $7.29m FY26, +19%; royalty/licence revenue $1.25m FY26, +17%, earned as legacy ingredient customers -- notably Probi AB in North America -- transition to Probi's own manufacturing) and separately sells its own finished consumer products (capsules, lozenges, dental SKUs) through NZ pharmacy wholesale, Amazon US, its own webstore, and cross-border e-commerce (CBEC) into China. FY26 revenue was $14.668m, up 16% on FY25's $12.644m, but reported EBITDA was only $0.9m (6% margin) after absorbing a disclosed $0.9m one-off supply-chain cost increase; underlying (adjusted) EBITDA was $1.8m. NPAT was $0.7m. Momentum accelerated sharply into FY27: the 20 August 2026 Q1 FY27 (three months to 30 June 2026) trading update reported record revenue of $5.1m (+42% YoY) and EBITDA of $1.1m profit versus a $0.2m loss in 1Q26, driven by B2B revenue up 67% (Asia Pacific ingredient growth, strong Probi royalties, and China private label sales, partly offset by weaker European ingredient revenue) while B2C revenue grew a more modest 4%. Management explicitly cautioned the quarter should not be annualised but reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 10-15% full-year revenue growth. The single most important commercial relationship remains Probi AB, a Swedish probiotics company that is simultaneously BLIS's largest licensee/customer, a top-3 (~13%) shareholder, and has a seat on the BLIS board (CEO Anita Johansen is a BLIS director) -- Probi-related-party revenue was $2.34m in FY26 (~16% of total revenue). Cash generated from operations was NEGATIVE $(0.6)m in FY26 (vs +$1.8m in FY25) despite positive NPAT, driven by an $862k inventory build and a $984k increase in trade receivables -- a working-capital drag that illustrates how quickly a small change in inventory/receivables can flip this business cash-flow negative, though the Q1 FY27 update suggests the supply-chain cost issue is now behind the company.

revenue_streams.name: B2B ingredient sales (bulk BLIS K12/M18 to manufacturers)
B2B private label / royalty & licence fees (incl. Probi)
B2C New Zealand wholesale (pharmacy, dental SKUs)
Other income (interest, grants)
revenue_streams.trend: declining as cash balance is used for growth

business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2B (ingredient manufacturers, consumer-brand licensees, one dominant related-party partner in Probi AB) and B2C (pharmacy/wholesale retail, e-commerce/Amazon, direct webstore); highly customer-concentrated -- the three largest customers accounted for $7.99m of $14.67m FY26 revenue (~54%), versus ~54% in FY25 also
business_model.geographic_mix: North America 31% ($4.5m), EMEA 30% ($4.35m), Asia Pacific ex-NZ 24% ($3.57m), New Zealand 15% ($2.24m) of FY26 revenue; Q1 FY27 update flagged continued Asia Pacific ingredient strength and China private-label growth against softer European ingredient revenue; manufacturing and all non-current assets are based in New Zealand (Dunedin)

main_competitors: Probi AB (Sweden) -- both BLIS's largest licensee/distribution partner AND an increasingly capable direct competitor as it internalises manufacturing of BLIS-derived and its own probiotic strains
Chr. Hansen / Novonesis (Denmark, post-merger probiotics giant) -- global-scale ingredient supplier with vastly greater R&D and manufacturing scale
Generic/commodity oral-health probiotic strain suppliers (particularly from China) competing on price in the ingredient channel
Numerous smaller finished-goods consumer probiotic brands in the B2C oral-health and immunity categories
competitive_position.market_position: Niche specialist in oral-cavity probiotic strains (BLIS K12, M18) with a long clinical publication history (20 publications relating to its strains highlighted in FY26, 17 conferences attended/presented at) but tiny in absolute scale (~$14.7m FY26 revenue, tracking toward high-teens millions in FY27) relative to global probiotics/nutraceutical ingredient suppliers. BLIS is largely a price-taker in a market it does not lead by scale, and its own largest commercial partner (Probi) is progressively taking over manufacturing and distribution in BLIS's most lucrative territory (North America), converting BLIS from a product supplier into a lower-margin royalty recipient there -- though royalty economics can carry higher margin than physical ingredient supply, partially offsetting the volume loss. Sell-side coverage (Forsyth Barr, issuer-sponsored, initiated ~September 2026) forecasts revenue reaching NZ$21.6m by FY29 with EBITDA improving to NZ$4.2m as mix shifts toward higher-margin B2B/royalty revenue.

moat_factors.factor: Patent portfolio and clinical evidence base
moat_factors.description: Two new patents granted in FY26 (antiviral applications of S. salivarius K12/M18, and prebiotic-sugar formulations), plus 20 publications relating to BLIS strains cited in FY26 and a 25-year track record of peer-reviewed clinical research (originating from Professor John Tagg's University of Otago research). This is a real, defensible scientific/IP asset relative to undifferentiated generic probiotic suppliers, and did prove valuable in FY26: BLIS successfully resolved a material patent dispute with Bluestone Pharma/Lactosan (joint ownership outcome, plus a five-year extension to the European supply agreement) and separately received a favourable FDA 'Letter of No Objection' (GRAS status) update in May 2026. However, patents are a wasting asset -- with 10-20 year amortisation lives disclosed in the accounts -- and BLIS's moat rests as much on trade secrets/know-how and its brand/publication reputation as on enforceable patent exclusivity, which is a materially weaker moat than a pharma-style composition-of-matter patent.

moat_factors.factor: Strategic distribution partnership with Probi AB
moat_factors.description: The October 2025 revised Technology Licence and Distribution Agreement extends Probi's EXCLUSIVE rights to BLIS K12/M18 across the USA, Canada and certain EMEA markets, and newly adds pet nutrition. Q1 FY27 results show 'strong Probi royalties' as a specific growth driver, suggesting the relationship is now delivering tangible upside. This gives BLIS access to a much larger commercial partner's sales/marketing network, but the exclusivity itself concentrates BLIS's most valuable territories behind a single counterparty that also has board representation and has been reducing its ingredient purchases from BLIS as it internalises manufacturing -- structurally still more managed transition than pure growth moat, though the FY27 royalty strength is a positive early signal.

BLIS K12 and M18 hold GRAS 'no objection' status with the FDA and various other jurisdictional approvals; the ongoing China regulatory pathway (a key clinical trial commenced in 2H26, expected complete 1H27) is a multi-year investment to unlock a large but currently CBEC/grey-market-dependent Chinese consumer opportunity. This is a genuine, hard-to-replicate barrier for new entrants but requires continuous capital and management attention.

BLIS relies on a single New Zealand fermentation supplier for its core strains; a technology/know-how transfer to an offshore fermentation supplier has been underway specifically because the company identified single-supplier concentration as a continuity risk. The FY26 result was directly hit by a disclosed $0.9m one-off supply chain cost increase, but the strong Q1 FY27 EBITDA turnaround (from a $0.2m loss to a $1.1m profit) suggests this cost pressure has now largely cycled through.

weaknesses: Extreme revenue and profit concentration in three customers (~54% of FY26 revenue), one of which (Probi AB) is also a major shareholder and board-represented related party -- a structural conflict-of-interest and bargaining-power risk, not merely a diversification risk

Nine years to grow revenue from $8.2m (FY19) to $14.7m (FY26) (a ~9% CAGR) while EBITDA margin has oscillated between -24% (FY22) and +20% (FY20), evidencing historically limited pricing power and high operating leverage that cuts both ways -- though Q1 FY27's step-change in both revenue growth and margin is the strongest quarter on record and, if sustained, would materially change this picture
Single product family dependency -- BLIS K12/M18 (and derivatives) are effectively the entire commercial base; no meaningfully diversified pipeline of new strains generating revenue today
Small absolute scale limits R&D, marketing and regulatory investment relative to global probiotics ingredient suppliers

Nano-cap illiquidity: ~1.28bn shares at a low absolute share price (~2.0-2.4 cents) means the NZ$0.001 minimum tick size remains a meaningful proportion (roughly 4-5%) of the share price itself, still raising effective trading costs and price granularity/noise even after the recent re-rating
No dividend paid; company retains all earnings under a full-reinvestment strategy, so there is no income return to offset equity risk

growth_drivers: Record Q1 FY27 momentum: revenue +42% YoY to $5.1m and EBITDA swinging from a $0.2m loss to a $1.1m profit, with B2B revenue +67% driven by Asia Pacific ingredient growth, Probi royalties and China private label sales

Expanded Probi AB agreement (Oct 2025) adds pet nutrition as a new licensed category across the USA, Canada and certain EMEA markets -- a genuinely new addressable market riding on Probi's existing commercial infrastructure, now showing up as 'strong Probi royalties' in Q1 FY27

China private label/offline professional health channel expansion -- private label revenue grew 67% in FY26 to $1.3m and Q1 FY27 flagged continued China private label strength, a structurally different (and potentially more durable) growth path than the declining CBEC/daigou channel

China regulatory pathway progressing to examination stage for BLIS K12/M18, with a pivotal clinical trial begun in 2H26 (due to complete 1H27) -- if successful, opens a large, currently under-monetised consumer market on a compliant footing rather than via grey-market resellers
New Zealand wholesale/pharmacy and dental SKU ranging showing strong repeat-purchase economics and continued shelf-space wins
Two new patents granted in FY26 (antiviral applications, prebiotic-sugar combination formulations) opening new product development avenues in immunity and broader health categories beyond oral care
FDA 'Letter of No Objection' (GRAS) update for BLIS K12 (May 2026) supports continued/expanded US market access

Sell-side (Forsyth Barr) forecasts revenue reaching NZ$21.6m by FY29 with EBITDA of NZ$4.2m as mix shifts toward higher-margin B2B/royalty revenue -- issuer-sponsored coverage, so directional rather than independent, but consistent with management's own reaffirmed 10-15% FY27 growth guidance

business.description: The three largest customers generated ~54% of FY26 revenue ($7.99m of $14.67m). Probi AB -- simultaneously BLIS's largest licensed distribution partner, a ~13% shareholder, and board-represented via CEO Anita Johansen -- alone contributed $2.34m of related-party revenue in FY26. Loss, renegotiation, or a change in strategy at any of these counterparties (particularly Probi, which has been steadily converting from ingredient purchaser to royalty payer as it internalises manufacturing) would be highly damaging and BLIS has limited practical ability to negotiate at arm's length given the governance overlap.

Commercial success rests almost entirely on the BLIS K12/M18 strain family; there is no meaningfully monetised pipeline of alternative strains today. A new competing strain, a safety/efficacy controversy, or a shift in consumer/scientific preference away from oral-cavity probiotics would remove the company's entire commercial basis.

business.risk: Historically thin, volatile EBITDA margins, with one strong quarter not yet proven durable
business.description: EBITDA margin ranged from -24% (FY22) to +20% (FY20) over FY19-26 and was only 6% in FY26 (8% underlying). Q1 FY27's ~22% EBITDA margin is a marked improvement, but management explicitly cautioned the quarter 'should not be annualised to a full year' and reaffirmed only the pre-existing 10-15% FY27 revenue growth guidance rather than raising it -- the historical pattern of high operating leverage cutting both ways has not yet been disproven over a full cycle.

Reliance on one New Zealand-based fermentation supplier caused a disclosed $0.9m one-off cost increase in FY26 that materially depressed reported EBITDA; a technology transfer to an offshore back-up supplier has been underway, and the Q1 FY27 margin recovery suggests progress, but full resolution is not yet confirmed.

business.risk: IP protection is a mix of patents, trademarks and trade secrets, not a single strong barrier
business.description: The FY26 resolution of the Bluestone Pharma/Lactosan dispute (ending in joint patent ownership rather than BLIS's sole ownership) illustrates that BLIS's patent estate is contestable and does not guarantee exclusivity; competitors and even historical customers can develop or acquire rights to adjacent IP.

financial.risk: Negative FY26 operating cash flow despite positive NPAT
financial.description: Cash generated from operations was $(0.6)m in FY26 versus NPAT of $0.7m, driven by an $862k inventory build and a $984k increase in trade receivables. Cash and short-term deposits fell from $9.7m to $8.5m over the year. While this appears to be a working-capital timing issue rather than a structural cash burn, the FY26 cash-conversion ratio of -64% (versus +178% in FY25) underlines how volatile and unpredictable cash generation is at this scale, and the trend statement shows negative operating cash flow in three of the last eight years (FY19, FY22, FY26).

financial.risk: Nano-cap illiquidity and tick-size distortion, though easing with the re-rating
financial.description: At a share price around NZ$0.02-0.024 with ~1.28 billion shares on issue (market cap roughly NZ$28-29m as of mid-September 2026), the standard NZX $0.001 minimum price increment still represents a meaningful 4-5% of the share price -- a structurally large bid-ask spread/step versus large caps that widens effective trading costs and can produce outsized percentage price swings on thin volume, even after the stock's ~29% 12-month gain.

financial.risk: No dividend and reliance on continued capital discipline
financial.description: Full-reinvestment policy means shareholders rely entirely on capital appreciation; with $8.5m cash and short-term deposits and no debt the balance sheet is solid, but there is no income cushion and the $4.3m unrecognised deferred tax asset (from $14.5m of gross tax losses) will only be realised if the company sustains profitability.

regulatory.description: BLIS's China regulatory pathway for K12/M18 remains mid-process (progressed to 'examination stage' in FY26, with a pivotal clinical trial begun in 2H26 and due to complete 1H27); approval timing and outcome are not guaranteed, and the interim reliance on cross-border e-commerce/daigou channels is itself being deliberately wound back, creating a gap between the old China model and the new compliant one -- though Q1 FY27 China private label strength suggests an alternative growth path is already gaining traction ahead of formal approval.

Amazon US revenue grew despite 'the increased tariff' per the FY26 Chair/CEO letter, and management stated minimal economic loss to date from Middle East conflict-related uncertainty, but ongoing US tariff policy is an explicit, acknowledged cost pressure on BLIS's direct-to-consumer US business.

regulatory.risk: Health/nutraceutical product liability and regulatory approval risk generally
regulatory.description: As a seller of health supplements and conductor of clinical trials, BLIS is exposed to product liability claims and the risk of losing regulatory approval to market/sell in specific countries, both explicitly identified as principal risks in the FY26 governance disclosures.

macro.description: Revenue is predominantly export-derived (85% of FY26 revenue from outside New Zealand) and denominated in USD, EUR and other currencies against an NZD cost base and functional currency; a 10% adverse FX move was modelled to reduce FY26 pre-tax surplus by $29k (disclosed sensitivity), and BLIS uses limited forward FX cover without formal hedge accounting.

B2C revenue is exposed to discretionary consumer spending on wellness/health supplements, which can soften in a weaker macro/consumer environment, particularly in the price-sensitive Amazon/US direct channel; Q1 FY27 B2C growth of only 4% (versus 67% B2B growth) illustrates this segment is currently the slower-growing, more cyclical half of the business.

Manufacturing, R&D and corporate costs are NZD-denominated in a small domestic economy with a thin specialist labour pool (fermentation science, regulatory affairs) that could face wage inflation pressure disproportionate to global peers with larger operations.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global probiotics/nutraceutical demand continues to grow structurally on consumer interest in gut, oral and immune health, but the industry is increasingly commoditised at the ingredient level with well-funded global players (Novonesis/Chr. Hansen, IFF/Danisco, Lallemand) competing on scale, cost and breadth of strain portfolios. BLIS's oral-cavity probiotic niche remains differentiated by its clinical evidence base but is small relative to the broader probiotics category.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate. B2C wellness/supplement spending has some discretionary sensitivity to consumer confidence; B2B ingredient revenue depends on customers' own order cycles and can be lumpy quarter to quarter (e.g. FY26 EMEA growth was partly attributed to order timing/shorter reorder cycles from one major customer, and Q1 FY27 showed a sharp swing between B2B strength and softer European ingredient demand), adding volatility beyond pure end-market demand cycles.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity given no debt, but BLIS earns meaningful interest income on its ~$8.5m cash/short-term deposit balance ($263k in FY26, down from $428k in FY25 as NZ rates eased and cash was drawn down) -- a modest earnings tailwind/headwind depending on the rate cycle.
key_input_costs: Fermentation/manufacturing (raw materials and consumables rose to $4.13m in FY26 from $2.56m, the single largest driver of margin compression, including the disclosed $0.9m one-off cost increase, though Q1 FY27 margin recovery suggests this has eased)
Marketing/advertising spend to support B2C brand awareness and Amazon advertising efficiency
Clinical trial and regulatory costs (China pathway, new product development)
Skilled scientific/regulatory affairs staff in a thin NZ labour market

recent_developments.event: Patent dispute with Bluestone Pharma GmbH (BSP) and Lactosan GmbH & Co. KG resolved: relevant patent applications became jointly owned by BLIS and BSP, all claims between the parties released, and a five-year extension to the existing European supply agreement was renegotiated, providing commercial continuity for the European ingredient relationship
Dame Alison Stewart assumed the role of Chair (following Geoff Plunket's retirement as Chair, and later as a director in March 2026)

Revised Technology Licence and Distribution Agreement with Probi AB announced: extends Probi's exclusive rights to BLIS K12 and BLIS M18 across the USA, Canada and certain EMEA markets, and for the first time adds pet nutrition to Probi's licensed territories

H1 FY26 (six months to 30 September 2025) results released: revenue $7.7m (+28% YoY), EBITDA $0.5m ($1.3m underlying, ex a disclosed $0.8m one-off supply chain cost increase), B2B revenue $5.3m (+39%), B2C revenue $2.4m (+10%); management guided full-year FY26 revenue growth of 10-15% on FY25 (actual FY26 growth came in at 16%, above the top of this range)
Paul Munro (former CEO of Christchurch City Holdings Limited, ex-Deloitte Corporate Finance Partner) appointed as an Independent Non-Executive Director
BLIS K12 received a 'Letter of No Objection' (GRAS self-affirmation confirmation) from the US FDA, reinforcing US market access for the ingredient

FY26 audited annual results released: revenue $14.668m (+16% YoY), reported EBITDA $0.9m (6% margin), underlying EBITDA $1.8m (+83% YoY, ex the $0.9m one-off supply chain cost), NPAT $0.7m (underlying NPAT $1.6m, +90% YoY), cash and short-term deposits $8.5m (down from $9.7m), cash generated from operations NEGATIVE $(0.6)m (driven by inventory build and receivables growth)

Q1 FY27 (three months to 30 June 2026) trading update: revenue $5.1m (+42% YoY, +$1.5m), EBITDA $1.1m profit (versus $0.2m loss in 1Q26), B2B revenue +67% (Asia Pacific ingredient growth, strong Probi royalties, China private label sales, partly offset by weaker European ingredient revenue), B2C revenue +4%; CEO Scott Johnson called it 'an exceptional start to the year, with record revenue and EBITDA' while cautioning the quarter should not be annualised, and reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 10-15% full-year revenue growth

2026 Annual Shareholders' Meeting held at the Dunedin Public Art Gallery (hybrid virtual/in-person); resolutions included the election of Paul Munro and an increase in the aggregate director remuneration pool from $309,000 to $340,000 per annum following external benchmarking

Forsyth Barr (in partnership with MST Access) initiated issuer-sponsored equity research coverage ('A Bacterial Growth Story'), forecasting revenue reaching NZ$21.6m by FY29 with improving mix lifting EBITDA to NZ$4.2m, and a blended peer-comparison valuation of approximately NZ$0.029 per share -- above the then-prevailing ~NZ$0.02-0.024 share price; note this is paid, issuer-sponsored research and should be read as directional rather than independent

Share price traded around NZ$0.02-0.024 (versus ~NZ$0.016-0.018 in mid-2026), with market capitalisation of roughly NZ$28-29m and 12-month share price performance of approximately +29%, reflecting the market's positive reaction to the Q1 FY27 trading update and improving underlying momentum

guidance.as_of: Q1 FY27 trading update (20 August 2026), reaffirming guidance first issued at the FY26 Annual Report (20 May 2026)

items.metric: Revenue growth (FY26, historical guidance already resolved)
items.vs_prior: achieved -- actual FY26 growth of 16% came in above the top end of the previously guided 10-15% range
items.notes: Guidance given at H1 FY26 (November 2025); FY26 actual revenue of $14.668m was +16.0% on FY25's $12.644m

CEO Scott Johnson reaffirmed this range at the 20 August 2026 Q1 FY27 trading update despite Q1 revenue growth of 42% YoY, explicitly cautioning that 'the first quarter should not be annualised to a full year' -- guidance was not raised even after a record quarter, suggesting management is being conservative about extrapolating one quarter's strength (particularly given one-off Probi royalty and China private-label timing effects)

items.metric: Q1 FY27 results (already reported, informs FY27 trajectory)
items.notes: Revenue $5.1m (+42% YoY), EBITDA $1.1m profit (vs $0.2m loss in 1Q26); unaudited

items.target: Approximately $0.1m of further one-off costs expected to be released
items.vs_prior: disclosed at H1 FY26; appears largely resolved based on the strong Q1 FY27 margin recovery
items.notes: Disclosed at H1 FY26 alongside the $0.8-0.9m one-off cost recognised; the Q1 FY27 EBITDA swing to profit is consistent with this cost pressure having substantially cycled through

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Scott Johnson (20 August 2026, Q1 FY27 update): 'We have had an exceptional start to the year, with record revenue and EBITDA. Although the first quarter should not be annualised to a full year, we are comfortable with our current forecast of 10%-15% revenue growth for FY27.' Earlier, Chair Dame Alison Stewart and CEO Scott Johnson at the FY26 annual report (May 2026): 'We enter FY27 with confidence. The combination of strengthened partnerships with our key business partners and growing B2B momentum provides a solid commercial foundation... We will maintain financial discipline and focus on delivering sustainable, profitable growth.' Management has flagged minimal economic impact to date from Middle East conflict-related macro uncertainty. No formal FY27 EBITDA or margin guidance range has been issued; the only explicit numeric target remains the 10-15% FY27 revenue growth range.

bull_case: Q1 FY27 delivered the strongest quarter in the company's history -- revenue +42% YoY and EBITDA swinging from a $0.2m loss to a $1.1m profit -- with management explicitly framing it as evidence the FY26 supply-chain cost drag and prior margin volatility are being worked through, and reaffirming (not merely defending) 10-15% FY27 revenue growth guidance

Genuine, differentiated scientific/IP base (20 publications relating to BLIS strains in FY26 alone, two new patents granted, 25-year clinical track record) that a purely commodity ingredient supplier would lack, supporting premium positioning in oral-health probiotics

Debt-free balance sheet with $8.5m cash and short-term deposits against a market cap of roughly NZ$28-29m -- cash still covers close to a third of the market capitalisation even after the recent re-rating, and a $4.3m unrecognised tax-loss asset provides a multi-year tax shield if sustained profitability is achieved

The Probi AB relationship, despite its concentration risk, is now delivering tangible upside -- 'strong Probi royalties' were a specific driver of Q1 FY27 B2B growth -- while giving BLIS access to a much larger partner's commercial infrastructure across the USA, Canada and EMEA, recently extended into a new pet-nutrition adjacency

Multiple option-value catalysts in progress -- China regulatory/clinical approval (trial due to complete 1H27), pet nutrition category expansion, and continued patent grants -- any one of which could be a step-change in addressable market if successful; issuer-sponsored Forsyth Barr coverage (initiated September 2026) forecasts revenue of NZ$21.6m and EBITDA of NZ$4.2m by FY29, implying a blended valuation (~NZ$0.029/share) above the recent trading range
bear_case: Nine years of revenue growth from $8.2m to $14.7m (roughly 9% CAGR) has not translated into consistent profitability: EBITDA margin was negative in FY22-23 and only 6% in FY26, and one strong quarter (Q1 FY27) does not yet establish a durable, scalable earnings trajectory -- management itself declined to raise FY27 guidance despite the beat, an implicit signal of caution about extrapolating the quarter

Extreme customer/related-party concentration: the top three customers are ~54% of FY26 revenue, and the single largest commercial partner (Probi AB) is simultaneously a ~13% shareholder with a board seat, creating both a governance conflict-of-interest and a structural risk that BLIS's best territories (North America, key EMEA markets) are being progressively ceded to a partner who is also internalising manufacturing away from BLIS -- Q1 FY27 already showed weaker European ingredient revenue alongside Probi royalty strength, exactly the mix-shift risk previously flagged

FY26 cash generated from operations was NEGATIVE $(0.6)m despite positive NPAT, driven by inventory build and receivables growth -- a reminder that reported profit at this scale can diverge sharply from actual cash generation, and cash/short-term deposits fell $1.2m over the year

Nano-cap illiquidity persists even after the re-rating (market cap ~NZ$28-29m, share price ~2.0-2.4 cents against ~1.28bn shares) with a $0.001 minimum tick still representing 4-5% of the share price, meaningfully widening effective trading costs and discouraging institutional ownership

Single product-family dependency on BLIS K12/M18 with no meaningfully monetised alternative-strain pipeline, combined with a track record of patent/IP disputes (the FY26 Bluestone Pharma/Lactosan resolution ended in shared rather than exclusive ownership) that shows the IP moat is contestable rather than absolute

No dividend, thin trading liquidity, and the only numeric FY27 target is the pre-existing 10-15% revenue growth range -- investors are being asked to underwrite continued execution (China approval, Probi joint business plans, sustained margin recovery) largely on the strength of a single quarter's results plus paid, issuer-sponsored analyst coverage rather than a longer independent track record of consistent execution
